rd.text:

tax.text:

da.text: Cost of goods and services sold includes personnel costs, manufacturing costs, raw materials and product costs, freight costs, depreciation, and facility costs associated with our manufacturing and warehouse facilities. wc.text: Working capital - Working capital at December 31, 2024 decreased by $276.9 million, or 21.9%, as compared to December 31, 2023, which includes an unfavorable foreign currency translation impact of $41.8 million. Excluding the impact of currency exchange rates, cash and cash equivalents, total current liabilities and inventories decreased by $349.0 million, $103.3 million and $42.0 million, respectively, while accounts receivable increased by $58.8 million. The decrease in cash and cash equivalents was due to capital expenditures and share repurchases in 2024 , offset by cash collections driven by positive operating results during the period. The decrease in total current liabilities was primarily due to the Company amending its Credit Facility Agreement during 2024. As part of this amendment, all current notes payable and other current debt amounts were repaid. The decrease in inventories and the increase in accounts receivable were both due to increased net sales leading up to the December 31, 2024 balance sheet date as compared to the December 31, 2023 balance sheet date.

net sales.heading: Net Sales
net sales.text:
Our net sales result from the sale of goods or services and reflect the net consideration which we expect to receive in exchange for those goods or services.

Several factors affect our reported net sales in any period, including product, payer and geographic sales mix, operational effectiveness, pricing realization, timing of orders and shipments, regulatory actions, competition, and business acquisitions that involve our customers or competitors.

The provision for income taxes was $121.6 million, $107.5 million, and $122.3 million for the years 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively, and the effective tax rate was 20.2%, 18.4%, and 17.5%, respectively.

The increase in the effective tax rate in 2025 of 1.8% is due primarily to a decrease in the tax benefit related to stock-based compensation in 2025, as compared to 2024 .

wc.text: Working capital - Working capital at December 31, 2025 increased by $335.6 million, or 34.0%, as compared to December 31, 2024, which includes an increase of $49.0 million due to foreign currency translation. Excluding the impact of currency exchange rates, cash and cash equivalents, total current liabilities, inventories and other current assets increased by $281.8 million, $75.7 million, $42.3 million and $45.2 million, respectively. The increase in cash and cash equivalents was due to cash from operations, partially offset by share repurchases and capital expenditures in 2025 . The increase in total current liabilities was driven by increases in our annual incentives. The increase in inventories was largely in work-in-progress and finished goods inventory in connection with customer demand to ensure we have sufficient inventory on hand to support the needs of our customers. The increase in other current assets was due primarily to held for sale assets being recorded into other current assets. For further information regarding the Company's held for sale assets at December 31, 2025 refer to Note 1, Basis of Presentation and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies .

net sales.heading: Net Sales
net sales.text:
Our net sales result from the sale of goods or services and reflect the net consideration which we expect to receive in exchange for those goods or services.

Several factors affect our reported net sales in any period, including product, payer and geographic sales mix, operational effectiveness, pricing realization, timing of orders and shipments, regulatory actions, competition, and business acquisitions that involve our customers or competitors.

Proprietary Products.text: Our business operations are organized into two global segments, Proprietary Products and Contract-Manufactured Products. Our Proprietary Products reportable segment offers proprietary packaging, containment solutions and drug delivery systems, along with analytical lab services and other integrated services and solutions, primarily to biologic, generic and pharmaceutical drug customers. Our Contract-Manufactured Products reportable segment serves as a fully integrated business, focused on the design, manufacture, and automated assembly of complex devices, primarily for pharmaceutical, diagnostic, and medical device customers. We also maintain collaborations to share technologies and market products with affiliates in Japan and Mexico.

The decrease in total current liabilities was primarily due to the Company amending its Credit Facility Agreement during 2024. As part of this amendment, all current notes payable and other current debt amounts were repaid. The decrease in inventories and the increase in accounts receivable were both due to increased net sales leading up to the December 31, 2024 balance sheet date as compared to the December 31, 2023 balance sheet date.

capex.text: Net cash used in investing activities increased by $10.0 million in 2024, due to an increase in capital expenditures for additional manufacturing capacity to meet future customer demand.

net sales.heading: Net Sales
net sales.text:
Our net sales result from the sale of goods or services and reflect the net consideration which we expect to receive in exchange for those goods or services.

Several factors affect our reported net sales in any period, including product, payer and geographic sales mix, operational effectiveness, pricing realization, timing of orders and shipments, regulatory actions, competition, and business acquisitions that involve our customers or competitors.

gp.heading: Gross Profit
gp.text:
The following table presents gross profit and related gross margins, consolidated and by reportable segment and by unallocated:

Consolidated gross profit increased by $105.5 million, or 10.6%, in 2025, including a favorable foreign currency translation impact of $25.5 million. Consolidated gross profit margin increased by 1.4 margin points in 2025.

Proprietary Products – Proprietary Products gross profit increased by $107.7 million, or 12.0%, in 2025, including a favorable foreign currency translation impact of $23.6 million. Proprietary Products gross profit margin increased by 1.9 margin points in 2025. The increase is due to increased customer demand, primarily of high value components, higher plant absorption and sales price increases. These increases were partially offset by approximately $47 million in customer incentives received in connection with volumes achieved during 2024 that were not repeated in the same period in 2025.

Contract-Manufactured Products – Contract-Manufactured Products gross profit decreased by $2.2 million, or 2.2%, in 2025. Contract-Manufactured Products gross profit margin decreased by 1.0 margin points in 2025, due primarily to increased production costs, partially offset by sales price increases.

rd.heading: Research and development expenses
rd.text:
Research and development expenses relate to our investments in improvements to our manufacturing processes, product enhancements, and additional investments in our elastomeric packaging components, formulation development, integrated drug containment systems, self-injection systems and drug administration consumables.

We expense research and development costs as incurred. Our research and development expenses fluctuate from period to period primarily based on the ongoing improvements to our manufacturing processes and product enhancements.

ga.heading: Selling, general and administrative expenses
ga.text: Selling, general and administrative expenses primarily include personnel costs, incentive compensation, insurance, professional fees, and depreciation.

sga.heading: Selling, general and administrative expenses
sga.text: Selling, general and administrative expenses primarily include personnel costs, incentive compensation, insurance, professional fees, and depreciation.

nonop.heading: Interest Expense, Net and Interest Income
nonop.text:
The following table presents interest expense, net, by significant component:

Interest expense, net, decreased by $2.5 million, or 83.3%, in 2025, due primarily to an increase in capitalized interest in 2025 and interest expense on repayments made on the Company's Series B notes in 2024 that was not repeated in 2025.

Interest income decreased by $2.1 million, or 10.7%, in 2025, due primarily to a decline in interest rates and the Company having a lower average cash balance in 2025, as compared to 2024 .

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text:
The provision for income taxes was $121.6 million, $107.5 million, and $122.3 million for the years 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively, and the effective tax rate was 20.2%, 18.4%, and 17.5%, respectively.

The increase in the effective tax rate in 2025 of 1.8% is due primarily to a decrease in the tax benefit related to stock-based compensation in 2025, as compared to 2024 .

Please refer to Note 17, Income Taxes , for further discussion of our income taxes.

net.text: Equity in net income of affiliated companies was $14.4 million, $14.7 million, and $17.7 million for the years 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively. Equity in net income of affiliated companies decreased by $0.3 million, or 2.0%, in 2025, due primarily to less favorable operating results at Daikyo and the Mexico affiliates.

ocf.heading: Net Cash Provided by Operating Activities
ocf.text: Net cash provided by operating activities increased by $101.4 million in 2025, due primarily to improved operating results and the timing of incentive payments.

da.text: Cost of goods and services sold includes personnel costs, manufacturing costs, raw materials and product costs, freight costs, depreciation, and facility costs associated with our manufacturing and warehouse facilities. Fluctuations in our cost of goods sold correspond with the fluctuations in sales units as well as inflationary and other market factors that influence our cost base.

sbc.text: During 2025, we recorded a tax benefit of $4.5 million associated with stock-based compensation.

wc.text: Working capital - Working capital at December 31, 2025 increased by $335.6 million, or 34.0%, as compared to December 31, 2024, which includes an increase of $49.0 million due to foreign currency translation. Excluding the impact of currency exchange rates, cash and cash equivalents, total current liabilities, inventories and other current assets increased by $281.8 million, $75.7 million, $42.3 million and $45.2 million, respectively. The increase in cash and cash equivalents was due to cash from operations, partially offset by share repurchases and capital expenditures in 2025 . The increase in total current liabilities was driven by increases in our annual incentives. The increase in inventories was largely in work-in-progress and finished goods inventory in connection with customer demand to ensure we have sufficient inventory on hand to support the needs of our customers. The increase in other current assets was due primarily to held for sale assets being recorded into other current assets. For further information regarding the Company's held for sale assets at December 31, 2025 refer to Note 1, Basis of Presentation and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies .

capex.text: Net cash used in investing activities decreased by $92.8 million in 2025, due primarily to a decrease in capital expenditures.

net sales.heading: Net Sales
net sales.text:
Our net sales result from the sale of goods or services and reflect the net consideration which we expect to receive in exchange for those goods or services.

Several factors affect our reported net sales in any period, including product, payer and geographic sales mix, operational effectiveness, pricing realization, timing of orders and shipments, regulatory actions, competition, and business acquisitions that involve our customers or competitors.

Proprietary Products.text: Our business operations are organized into two global segments, Proprietary Products and Contract-Manufactured Products. Our Proprietary Products reportable segment offers proprietary packaging, containment solutions and drug delivery systems, along with analytical lab services and other integrated services and solutions, primarily to biologic, generic and pharmaceutical drug customers. Our Contract-Manufactured Products reportable segment serves as a fully integrated business, focused on the design, manufacture, and automated assembly of complex devices, primarily for pharmaceutical, diagnostic, and medical device customers. We also maintain collaborations to share technologies and market products with affiliates in Japan and Mexico.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
